In order to calculate \[\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}\] we need to express \[{{CT:0}}\] as the sum of its partial fractions <hint>alg_partial_fractions</hint>.

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:3}}{{CT:4}} + {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}}
 \end{array}\]

By multiplying both sides by {{CT:7}} we get

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
{{CT:8}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}}+{{CT:10}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}}
 \end{array}\]

Equating coefficients of {{CT:12}} we get a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = 1\) and \(B = 1\).

So, \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:13}}\]

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:13}} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}} + \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}} +c
 \end{array}\]
